key_insight: A quantics tensor-train (QTT) Chebyshev-Galerkin method solves global spectral boundary-value systems directly in compressed form while preserving their variational structure.
engineering_relevance: The approach enables accurate elasticity analysis across large design and uncertainty spaces, with computational cost governed by tensor compressibility rather than unknown count alone.
method: Assemble weak-form Chebyshev-Galerkin operators directly in QTT format without forming full arrays.
Handle coupled elliptic systems, variable coefficients, mapped geometries, and mixed Dirichlet-Robin conditions.
Treat parameters and random inputs as extra coordinates to solve entire parameter spaces at once.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports errors below 10⁻⁸ on a 3D elasticity benchmark, 1.7×10⁷ cantilever designs solved in 92 seconds, and 2.4×10⁶-fold memory reduction versus a full stochastic coefficient array.
watch_item: Efficiency depends on QTT compressibility; performance for poorly compressible fields or geometries remains a concern beyond the reported benchmarks.
paper_title: A Tensor-Network Chebyshev-Galerkin Method for Boundary-Value Problems in Computational Mechanics
